Cut The Lights.bio: Cut The Lights is a Toronto hip-hop group fronted vocally by Rochester, the Toronto rapper also known as Rochester Juice. The group has released tracks including 'Run,' 'Too Bright' and 'Back It Up,' and Rochester has described Cut The Lights as his group while discussing its placements in projects including Across the Spider-Verse, Fortnite and NFL Films. Northern Dial carries Cut The Lights as part of its contemporary Toronto hip-hop catalogue.

Calibur.bio: Calibur is the hip-hop stage name used by Ajax vocalist Najja Crest, who emerged from Durham Region's early-2000s music scene after performing with the groups Foot Soldiers and Bush Life. A contemporary Pickering-area profile identifies Najja 'Calibur' Crest as an Ajax artist who had opened for acts including Boot Camp, Jeru and Ghetto Concept. Northern Dial carries Calibur as part of its Durham Region and Canadian hip-hop catalogue.

Lokz.bio: Lokz is the former stage name of Toronto singer, songwriter and producer Yuri Koller. Koller built his early career in Toronto under the Lokz name, appearing on JD Era's 'No Handouts,' performing at Toronto showcases and earning a slot at the first OVO Fest before later recording under his birth name. Northern Dial carries Lokz as part of its Toronto hip-hop and R&B catalogue.

Sugar Prince.bio: Sugar Prince is a Canadian old-school hip-hop artist associated with Vancouver's early-2000s rap scene. He appears with Jah-Fus on the Rascalz track 'Clash (We Don't Play)' from the Vancouver group's 2002 album 'Reloaded' and is catalogued among Canadian old-school hip-hop artists. Northern Dial carries Sugar Prince as part of its classic Canadian hip-hop catalogue.

Lotus James.bio: Lotus James is a Canadian hip-hop artist associated with the Lunch Room Poetz collective and the Greater Toronto underground scene. HipHopCanada featured Lotus James in the group's 'LRP Cypher,' describing the lineup as representing Canadian hip-hop, and he has continued to appear on Toronto-area releases through Motive Music Canada. Northern Dial carries Lotus James as part of its contemporary Canadian underground hip-hop catalogue.
